fact: Burundi's Senate voted unanimously to ratify the EAC protocol on Regional Digital Integration; the article is dated 2025-01-21 and gives no vote date, so the publication date is used.

fact: Burundi formally entered the EAC One Network Area on 1 August 2024, with new regulations from its regulator cutting regional roaming tariffs, so calls and data roaming with five other countries are treated as domestic rates.
The EACO report lists Burundi among its seven member states, with Burundi's regulator ARCT submitting data; the report gives no date for membership, so its publication date is used.

EACO reports Burundi's inbound One Network Area voice traffic rose 126% in 2025, from 89.6 million to 202.9 million minutes, and outbound rose 82.4% from 12.1 million to 22.1 million, attributing the rise to Burundi's accession to the ONA roaming framework and reduced roaming tariffs.

Burundi took part in the EAC Digital for Development Forum in Arusha on 23-24 June 2026, its delegation led by the director general of the digital economy programme at the finance ministry, who spoke on a cross-border digital public services panel.

The EAC press release on its 2026 Digital for Development Forum, which advances the EAC digital transformation agenda, names the Republic of Burundi among the eight EAC Partner States; the as_of is the document's published date, as it gives no date for membership.

The EAC release on the Meeting of the Technical Committee on Telecommunications, held in Dar es Salaam on 25 to 29 May 2026 to review a draft Regional Mobile Roaming Framework, brings together Partner States and names the Republic of Burundi among the EAC's eight members; it does not single out Burundi's delegation.

Burundi Times reports that an EAC and IGAD joint workshop on the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project in Nairobi treated Burundi among the region's countries, rating its data protection systems 'nascent' alongside Somalia, South Sudan and the DRC.
